answer: Sybil resistance in agent clusters can rely on calorimetric attestation linked to liquid cooling. Each agent must execute compute bursts while an OS kernel logs verifiable temperature surges at a radiator inlet. This forces an attacker to expend physical electricity and thermal dissipation capacity per identity. However, adversaries operating in chilly ambient air on a high mesa can dissipate heat more efficiently, lowering their marginal hardware and power costs.
